THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The present appeal is filed by the appellants/claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 06.08.2018 in MVC.No.29/2018 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC and MACT,
Periyapatna, for seeking enhancement of compensation.

2. Brief facts of the case are that, on 20.04.2017 around 1.00 pm., when the deceased was walking on the extreme left side of B.M.Road in front of Kannambadi Amma Temple, Periyapatna, the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-09-HC-1363, coming from Hunsur towards Periyapatna came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased.
Due to which, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

3. Heard the arguments from both sides and perused the records.
4.

The Tribunal has awarded the compensation under various heads as follows:
1 Loss of dependency Rs. 9,75,000/- 2 Loss of consortium, love Rs. 40,000/-
and affection 3 Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-

2 4 Transportation of dead body Rs. 15,000/- and funeral expenses 5

Medical expenses of the Rs.
3,12,000/-
 deceased during  hospitalization  TOTAL Rs. 13,57,000/-
5.
The deceased was aged 46 years as on the date of the accident and was an agriculturist and was earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.

The Tribunal has taken the income of the deceased at Rs.7,500/- pm.,
which is on the lower side.
As the accident is of the year 2017, notional income is to be taken at Rs.11,000/- pm., as per the Notional Income Chart recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co.,
Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi1 as the deceased was aged 46 years as on the date of the accident, 25% of income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life.

sentences.text: The claimants are wife and children of the deceased.
1/3rd of income is deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
As the deceased was aged 46 years as on the date of the accident, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '13'.
Hence, the compensation under the head loss of dependency is re-assessed and quantified as follows:
Accordingly, compensation of Rs.14,29,999/- which is rounded off to Rs.14,30,000/- is awarded under the head loss of dependency.
6. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium, love and affection, which is not correct.
As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Limited v. Nanu Ram & Others2, each claimants are entitled for Rs.40,000/- with 10% escalation.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Limited v. Nanu Ram & Others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, in the present case, there are three dependants.

Therefore,
compensation of Rs.1,32,000/- (Rs.40,000/- x 3 dependants = Rs.1,20,000/- + 10% escalation) is awarded under the head loss of consortium including loss of love and affection.
The compensation of Rs.3,12,000/- awarded under the head medical expenses of the deceased during hospitalization is as per the actual bills produced.
Hence, it is kept in tact.

8. The compensation of Rs.16,500/-

3 (Rs.15,000/- + 10% escalation) is awarded under the head loss of estate as against Rs.15,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

9. The compensation of Rs.16,500/-
(Rs.15,000/- + 10% escalation) is awarded under the head transportation of dead body and funeral expenses as against Rs.15,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

10. Thus, in all the appellants/claimants are entitled to the compensation as follows:
1 Loss of dependency Rs. 14,30,000/- 2 Loss of consortium Rs. 1,32,000/-
including loss of love and affection 3 Loss of estate Rs. 16,500/-
4 Transportation of dead Rs. 16,500/-
 body and funeral  expenses 5

Medical expenses of the Rs. 3,12,000/- Kept in tact  deceased during  hospitalization  TOTAL Rs. 19,07,000/-
11.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.13,57,000/-, but the appellants/claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.19,07,000/-.
Hence, the appellants/claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.5,50,000/- (Rs.19,07,000/- - Rs.13,57,000/-).

Therefore, the appellants/claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.5,50,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

12. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed-in-part.

ii. The impugned judgment and award dated *06.08.2018 in MVC.No.29/2018 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC and MACT, Periyapatna* is modified to the extent that the appellants/claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.5,50,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
iii. No order as to costs.
